html:
The Chisos were an Indigenous people of the desert and mountains of the Big Bend country, in northeastern Chihuahua and nearby Coahuila and Texas. The Chisos Mountains in Big Bend National Park keep their name. They were probably related to the Concho and may have spoken a Uto-Aztecan language, but little of it was recorded.

They hunted, gathered desert plants and raided Spanish settlements in northern New Spain in the late 1600s. In the 1700s they faded from the records, absorbed by missions or by the Mescalero Apache, who moved into the region. Neighbours: Tobosos and Jumanos. See also Chisos.
